analysis.title: US Midterm Review - Blue wave political ramifications
key_insights: Democrats appear to have flipped 7-8 Senate seats. They have won 54 seats and are on track for 55-56 in the new Senate. Pre-election expectation was 52-53 seats.
Alaska and Mississippi are not yet called, but tentative results point to Democratic wins. Mississippi is very close and would be the biggest Senate surprise, since Republicans were heavy favourites.
In the House, Democrats are on track for a large majority. Prediction markets price up to 260 seats, nearly 60%, against 218 needed.
Democrats flipped several close governor races: Georgia (expected), Ohio (toss-up), Texas and Kansas (both favoured for the GOP). Trump has said he will accept the result.

Danske does not expect the result to significantly change the fiscal policy outlook, so the impact on growth should be limited. CBO estimates 90% of the expected spending increase over the next decade comes from social security, healthcare costs and rising interest payments.
Danske sees a low chance of either party passing significant entitlement cuts before the 2028 elections, and a divided Congress makes that harder.

Divided government makes fiscal policy more predictable. Democratic majorities in both chambers mean Republicans cannot pass further deficit-widening reconciliation bills, and Trump's suggested USD 5,000 dividend for adults should be off the table.
Democrats cannot reach a two-thirds majority in both chambers, so Trump can veto Congress-initiated spending bills. Danske sees the fiscal stance as essentially locked in for 2027-28.
Markets will likely focus on the implications for the data centre buildout after Democratic challengers unseated Republican incumbents in the Texas, Georgia and Ohio governor races.

The outgoing Congress aims to pass full-year government funding before the stopgap bill expires on 11 December. Failure would force negotiation with House Democrats, risking repeated shutdowns in early 2027 and political concessions by Republicans.
Danske flags a possible more aggressive presidential push against Fed Governor Cook, and possible departures of some Republican-nominated Supreme Court justices before the new Congress sits.
